response.text:
# Fire-Department Training Card: Padlock Removal (Authorized Rescue)

**Purpose:** Standardized procedure for forcibly removing a padlock during an authorized rescue or emergency entry.

---

## 1. Scene Authorization

- [ ] Confirm rescue authorization from incident commander or officer in charge
- [ ] Verify legal authority to force entry (emergency condition, occupant unresponsive, life hazard)
- [ ] Attempt keys, combination retrieval, or lock-smith contact **before** cutting, when time permits
- [ ] Document authorization: time, authorizing officer, and reason for entry
- [ ] Confirm no alternate entry point is available with less damage

## 2. Personal Protective Equipment

- [ ] Full structural PPE or duty gloves appropriate for forcible-entry operations
- [ ] Eye protection: full-face shield or safety goggles (mandatory — flying metal fragments are the primary hazard)
- [ ] Helmet with face shield down before cutting begins
- [ ] Check gloves for cuts or compromised palms before gripping cutters

## 3. Bystander Clearance

- [ ] Establish an exclusion zone of at least 10 feet in all directions from the cut point
- [ ] Assign one member to control the area and verbally clear bystanders before each cut
- [ ] Announce "CLEAR" and receive confirmation before applying force
- [ ] Account for ricochet direction — fragments travel along the plane of the cut
- [ ] Keep other crew members out of the shackle's "whip zone" if the cut ends spring apart

## 4. Safe Bolt-Cutter Positioning

- [ ] Select cutters rated for the shackle diameter and hardness (typically 24-inch minimum for hardened shackles)
- [ ] Position the shackle deep in the jaw, against the throat of the cutters for maximum leverage
- [ ] Align the cutting edge perpendicular to the shackle — angled cuts slip and spray fragments
- [ ] Grip with both hands; keep fingers clear of the jaw path
- [ ] Brace your stance: feet shoulder-width, body balanced, cutting stroke directed **away** from your body and any crew member
- [ ] Cut the side of the shackle under **tension** (the side away from the lock body) — this side fails more readily
- [ ] Expect the shackle to snap and release stored energy; control the tool through the full stroke
- [ ] After the cut, control both cut ends — they may be sharp and under spring tension

## 5. Post-Operation

- [ ] Report entry made and conditions found to command
- [ ] Photograph or document the removed lock if required by department policy
- [ ] Inspect cutters for chipped or damaged jaws before re-stowing
- [ ] Debrief any tool failure or unexpected fragment behavior for the training record

---

**Note:** This card addresses authorized emergency forcible entry only. It does not cover covert, stealth, or non-consensual entry methods, which are outside the scope of fire-service rescue operations.
